column11: Kiddushin 39b: ‘The Gemara asks: But didn’t Rabbi Elazar say that those on the path to perform a mitzva are not susceptible to harm, neither when they are on their way to perform the mitzva nor when they are returning from performing the mitzva? column13: One who performs a mitzvah in order to receive a reward and for his own benefit, in an Israelite he is called "a complete tzaddik"; whereas among the nations of the world he is considered to have spoiled the deed through this; and so [in Bava Batra 10b], that it is reckoned a sin for them when they act solely for self-aggrandizement and the like, because with them this selfish thought is the primary essence; for which reason with them an evil thought is combined with deed while a good thought is not, as stated in the Yerushalmi [Peah 1:4] and Tosafos [Kiddushin 39b], whereas with Israel the opposite is true.

column13: And behold, the soul of man is commensurate solely with the thought and wisdom within man, for in this lies man's superiority over the beast; for otherwise, all vital vegetative and animate faculties exist equally in animals, and an animalistic soul would likewise have sufficed for man, were it not that the human soul was joined within him, which endows him with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge, wherefore we can define the essential soul as nothing other than an emanated faculty of wisdom and thought.
column15: For certainly the Blessed Name never destroys, but continually builds, as in Midrash Tehillim (75): “‘Al Tashchet (Destroy not)...’ Moses pleaded: Destroy not; the Holy One replied: I do not destroy, I build”; and as instituted in prayer: “Blessed is He who spoke and the world was.” However, from Abraham our Father onward an even higher reality began: the enduring existence of the cosmos was fortified through the legal mechanism of acquisition by physical pulling (meshichah)—the supreme mode of transaction after which no retraction is possible.

column15: So said the Holy One, blessed be He: “If I create the world with Mercy, sins will multiply; if with Justice, how can it endure? column11: Isaiah 45:18: ‘For thus said GOD,The Creator of heaven who alone is God,Who formed the earth and made it,Who alone established it—Who did not create it a waste,But formed it for habitation:I am GOD, and there is none else.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Isaiah 45:18) to illuminate his exposition here (“this being the holy increase of Israel, for which the world was created: "He created it not a waste" [Isaiah 45:18], never saying to Jacob's seed "Seek Me in vain" [ibid. 45:19]; but that existence endure eternally:...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And likewise, even those elite individuals must also recite the section of VeHaya Im Shamoa, just as they said to Rabbi Shimon bar Yochai in Shabbat 33b that he should return to the cave, for living in utter detachment is possible only within a cave and detached from ordinary worldly life. column15: And Israel illuminates this very darkness. column11: Isaiah 45:19: ‘I did not speak in secret,At a site in a land of darkness;I did not say to the stock of Jacob,“Seek Me out in a wasteland”—I GOD, who foretell reliably,Who announce what is true.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Isaiah 45:19) to illuminate his exposition here (“never saying to Jacob's seed "Seek Me in vain" [ibid. 45:19]; but that existence endure eternally: preservation in the species revealed in this world, and individual bodily resurrection in the Future, revealing that...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: Yet is not consumed by the harsh severity of awe, as it is written Isaiah 45:19: "I said not to the seed of Jacob who cling to the middle axis, 'Seek Me in chaos'": chaos refers to the green line the hue of tekhelet, signifying awe which encircles the entire universe. Nor does it abide exclusively in the overwhelming rush of love, rather along the lines of "Habakkuk came and established them upon one principle: 'And the righteous shall live by his faith'" Makkot 24a—.
column15: And indeed, ontologically the primordial darkness is rooted higher than light, as it is written (Isaiah 45:7): “Former of light and Creator of darkness,” and Beriah (Creation) is spiritually higher than Yetzirah (Formation), as taught in the Zohar (Terumah 155a): Beriah is to the Left and Yetzirah to the Right.

column15: And in this world, man attains merely a glimmer from the deep reserves of light that the Blessed Name is destined to reveal in the future; just as the Targum renders “A Song of Ascents” (Psalms 120:1): “to bring up the waters of the deep,” which means that the subterranean deep ascends to moisten and vitalize the world, as stated in the Gemara (Sukkah 53a): “The higher it rises, the more the earth is saturated.”

column11: Bava Batra 16a: ‘Reish Lakish says: Satan, the evil inclination, and the Angel of Death are one, that is, they are three aspects of the same essence. He is also the evil inclination, as it is written there: “The impulse of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continuously” (Genesis 6:5); and it is written here: “Only upon himself do not put forth your hand” (Job 1:12). The verbal analogy between the various uses of the word “only” teaches that the evil inclination is to be identified with the Satan. He is also the Angel of Death,…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Bava Batra 16a) to illuminate his exposition here (“And death serves only to consume the serpent's defilement, the serpent's skin, the inclination being the Angel of Death (Bava Batra 16a), for evil ever consumes itself; and this defilement exists perforce in all...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: Or if the sin is committed with immense passion, where the angel's power is likewise charged with intense passion, it nonetheless remains confined to the World of Asiyah through the act. Except that it is categorized into three impure husks (kelipot): 'stormy wind, etc.', for these are the three head-forces of evil: envy, lust, and honor; envy being a literal stormy wind in the heart churning and turbulent; and lust being the depth of darkness which completely obscures true holy yearning.
column15: And furthermore: surely even prior to this He knew that the inclination of man's heart is evil, why then were they punished with annihilation? However, the essential rationale lies in the word “from his youth” (mi-ne'urav): for a person’s inclination rages most intensely during the days of youth, when the force of bodily desire is wildly unruly, expanding into base cravings in an unchecked torrent, to the point where it is not within man's independent power through ordinary free will to place a bridle and bit upon his spirit, save through the antidote created by Hashem against it.

column13: And this explains the proof deduced from the verse: "For He will give His angels charge [over you]," that commandments possess the static steadfastness of angels, teaching that the one guarded is greater than the guardian, matching the superiority of the initiator over the effect; for since man possesses the potency to generate and activate this very force—which is the guardian force that knows no deviation, as King David, peace be upon him, proclaimed: "and my heart is slain within me" [Psalms 109:22], which the Sages expounded (Jerusalem Talmud, Berakhot 9:5) that he slew his evil inclination.
column15: In truth, goodness existed in this tree as well, but while in other trees good was clearly distinguishable from evil, in this tree good appeared as evil, defying easy discernment. column11: Rosh Hashanah 25a: ‘§ The Gemara relates that Rabbi Ḥiyya once saw the waning moon standing in the sky on the morning of the twenty-ninth of the month. He took a clump of earth and threw it at the moon, saying: This evening we need to sanctify you, i.e., the new moon must be visible tonight so that we may declare the thirtieth of the month as the New Moon, and you are still standing here? Go and cover yourself for now, so that the new moon will be seen only after nightfall. The Gemara further relates that Rabbi Yehuda HaNasi once said to Rabbi Ḥiyya: Go to a place called Ein Tav and sanctify the New Moon there, and send me a sign that you have sanctified it. The sign is: David, king of Israel, lives and…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 5, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Rosh Hashanah 25a) to illuminate his exposition here (“concerning whom they affirmed: "David king of Israel lives and endures" [Rosh Hashanah 25a], who died not, and "my flesh also shall dwell in safety" [Psalms 16:9], worms having no power over him, having stripped the...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: King David being the root of the moon's light, which is likewise light (Pesachim 2a); as stated in Rosh Hashanah (25a): "Send me the sign: David king of Israel lives and endures"; this being the code for sanctifying the New Moon as it begins to illuminate; and though the moon wanes, the eclipse exists only for the inhabitants of earth; while in its essential body its light endures forever, receiving uninterrupted rays from the sun.

column15: “And the sons of Noah, that went forth of the ark, were Shem, and Ham, and Japheth.” In Tanchuma (Noach 17): “‘And the sons of Noah were (vayihyu)’—that the Holy One, blessed be He, established for them enduring existence (havayah) in the world; whereas regarding the early generations He states (Ezekiel 26:21): ‘I will make you a terror, and you shall be no more; though you be sought for, yet shall you never be found again’ — ‘I will make you a terror’—as if they never were; ‘and you shall be no more’—now in this world; ‘though you be sought for’—in the World of Souls; ‘yet shall you never be found again’—in the World to Come.

column11: Yevamot 65b: ‘MISHNA: A man is commanded with regard to the mitzva to be fruitful and multiply, but not a woman. column13: And according to this, no difficulty arises from the verse "And God blessed them," wherein He addressed both of them with "be fruitful and multiply" (Yevamot 65b): for it was only when woman was stricken with the curse "and he shall rule over you" that she entered the status of deficiency, as explained above [and this occurred because she caused the introduction of mortality into the world, which is a deficiency in the very spiritual form of Man; unlike eating and reproduction which are merely physical characteristics of matter; therefore she was penalized measure for measure to become the embodiment of deficiency].

column15: “These are the generations of Noah, etc.” In Midrash Tanchuma (at the beginning of the parashah): “Let our master teach us: for how many transgressions do women die during childbirth? column11: Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 1: ‘Why were women enjoined to perform these three duties? The Holy One, blessed be He, said: Adam, the first of My creatures, was commanded not to eat the fruit of the tree of knowledge, yet concerning Eve, it is written: And when the woman saw that the tree was good for food … she gave also unto her husband with her and did eat (Gen. 3:6). In that way she brought about his death and, as it were, shed his blood, and the law prescribes: Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed (Gen. 9:6). That is why woman’s blood is made to flow. She is required to abstain from sexual relations during menstruation to atone for the blood of Adam that she was responsible for shedding.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Midrash Tanchuma, Noach 1) to illuminate his exposition here (“the true offspring of the righteous being Torah and mitzvot [Tanchuma Noach 1]. column13: Wherefore he could speak with Rebbe no further concerning dining with him. And there it is recorded that Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair cried: "Sons of the town, draw near to me! column15: And they said that it would be better for them to be left in the hands of His blessed will, without any power of free choice at all, through the laws of nature engraved in each and every one, about which they were confident that no flaw or deficiency would be found in them, for they have a claim, as stated (Ta’anit 20b): “Go to the Craftsman who made me.”

column15: And their creation is purely beneficial, so they naturally consent, for one may act in someone's favor without their presence. column15: “And now nothing will be withholden from them, which they purpose to do.” In Midrash Rabbah (38:9): This teaches that the Holy One opened for them a portal of repentance, as said: “And now (ve'atah)”—and “ve'atah” signifies repentance, as it is said (Deuteronomy 10:12): “And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear”; yet they said “No”; whereupon the Holy One declared: “Nothing shall be cut off/withheld from them that they purpose to do.”

And our holy Patriarchs stood continually facing Hashem face-to-face; therefore he did not circumcise himself until he received an explicit divine command, Hashem hinting that He left this realm for man to fence in and rectify himself.

column11: Sanhedrin 93b: ‘The Gemara asks from another perspective: Granted, according to the one who says that they were literally eunuchs, that is as it is written in the next verse: “And to them I will give in My house and within My walls a memorial better than sons and daughters: I will give him an everlasting name, that shall not be excised” (Isaiah 56:5). column13: For then one merits the completion of the Oral Torah, channeling Lower Wisdom from Supernal Wisdom; receiving a spirit from the Supernal Sanctuary through the perfection of fear in his heart, meriting that "the fear of Hashem is wisdom"; and from this he attains consummate holiness, being consecrated from on High; infusing holiness into all his physical bodily actions and the desires of the yetzer; which is impossible save through the perfection of Torah which flavors the yetzer as an antidote.
column15: With Israel, however, it is written: “And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear” — demanding that they first clarify through their own active labor the root of unity within them, after which Hashem sets His permanent seal, dwelling among them in Jerusalem. And this explains Yoma (9b): “Regarding the Second Temple, whose sin was not openly manifest, their end of exile was not revealed; and why were they exiled? Because of baseless hatred (sin'at chinam).”

column15: And therefore throughout the creation narrative the Name Elohim alone is written, denoting awe and constriction, which was missing in the earlier shattered worlds. And as taught by the Kabbalists, that the Shattering of the Vessels (Shevirat HaKelim) occurred, dissolving them; for the vessel is holy awe, as it is written (Isaiah 33:6): “The fear of the Lord is His treasure”; and because they lacked the awe which is the receptive vessel, they shattered completely.

column13: For then awakens annually that light present at Sinai during the first two commandments, which was the prototype of the future rectification; from whose energy issues the sanctity of the Two Loaves; wherefore they channel blessing unto the fruits of the tree which all draw sustenance from the Tree of Knowledge; and through the Two Loaves is imparted the power to transform the Tree of Knowledge into the Tree of Life; and through this is drawn down the blessing of children (banei).
column15: And the essential foundation of this vessel is the fear of Hashem, as it is written (Isaiah 33:6): “The fear of the Lord is His treasure”; meaning whoever toils in this world to magnify the honor of Hashem, which is currently obscured, in the future when “the whole earth is filled with His glory,” the determining factor will be: whoever prepared a larger vessel will absorb a greater measure of light.

column11: Bava Batra 12a: ‘§ In connection with Rabbi Yosei’s statement that Sumakhos’s words are nothing but words of prophecy, the Gemara reports that Rabbi Avdimi from Haifa says: From the day that the Temple was destroyed prophecy was taken from the prophets and given to the Sages. The Gemara expresses astonishment: Is that to say that a Sage is not fit to be a prophet? Rabbi Avdimi seems to say that these are two distinct categories of people. The Gemara explains: This is what Rabbi Avdimi is saying: Even though prophecy was taken from the prophets, it was not taken from the Sages.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Bava Batra 12a) to illuminate his exposition here (“for that which lives in the hearts of Israel's scholars—where "a sage is superior to a prophet" (Bava Batra 12a)—is the Oral Torah; whereas the Written Torah, descending through Moses from Supernal Wisdom, had its...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And what the Yefeh To'ar argued that Caleb should have suspected a temporary necessity—is entirely incorrect: for a temporary crisis applied only to Obadiah in the generation of Ahab when Jezebel slaughtered the prophets of Hashem, leaving no righteous man worthy save him; but in the generation of Joshua and Caleb, where all Israel were the righteous disciples of Moshe Rabbeinu, how could it enter your mind that a crisis would require the Holy Spirit to rest upon a slave or mamzer?!
column15: While the gentile demanding unearned indulgence cries “feed me of the fat-tail,” seeking pleasure without preliminary refinement, exposing his identity. For concerning Israel it is written: “And now, Israel, what does the Lord your God require of you, but to fear”—demanding deliberate refinement. So here: the generation of the Dispersion was budding, desiring the settlement of the world, wherefore Noah sought to banish anger to stabilize society — the reverse of the Flood generation who cared nothing for civilization, content with fleeting pleasure.

column11: Menachot 29b: ‘Moses said before God: Master of the Universe, show him to me. God said to him: Return behind you. Moses went and sat at the end of the eighth row in Rabbi Akiva’s study hall and did not understand what they were saying. Moses’ strength waned, as he thought his Torah knowledge was deficient. When Rabbi Akiva arrived at the discussion of one matter, his students said to him: My teacher, from where do you derive this? Rabbi Akiva said to them: It is a halakha transmitted to Moses from Sinai. When Moses heard this, his mind was put at ease, as this too was part of the Torah that he was to receive.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Menachot 29b) to illuminate his exposition here (“And over this Moses rejoiced when hearing Rabbi Akiva's disciples ask "From where do you derive this?" and Akiva replied "It is a halakhah given to Moses from Sinai" [Menachot 29b]; for everything Rabbi Akiva...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.

column13: And so from the perspective of their own identity they are termed dead even now. column15: And likewise with “Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One (Echad)” (Deuteronomy 6:4)—if you turn the Dalet into a Reish [saying Acher / other], removing the crownlet-corner of the Dalet, you destroy the world. He replied: From the circuit of the altar, as we learned in the Mishnah: “And he comes to the southeastern horn (keren), etc.”

column11: Chagigah 13b: ‘The verse states: “And I looked and, behold, a stormy wind came out of the north, a great cloud, with a fire flashing up, so that a brightness was round about it; and out of its midst was like the color of electrum, out of the midst of the fire” (Ezekiel 1:4). The Gemara poses a question: Where did that wind go? Rav Yehuda said that Rav said: It went to conquer the entire world under the wicked Nebuchadnezzar. And why was all of this necessary? Why was it necessary that the entire world be subjected to his dominion? column13: And one whose motive is not lust arrives at foreign thoughts solely through mocking and scoffing at the words of the Sages; for this is the root of Amalek, the first of the nations, who is called a "scorner" (leitz), whence expand subsequently all manners of idolatries of all the pagan nations; for through cynicism in the brain the entire body is rendered as excrement, the brain becoming a privy where food dross is excreted.
column15: And this is the distinction: regarding the legions of the Tabernacle, according to their exertion in service, so did they attain holiness; whereas the legions of the Torah transcend human labor, stemming from a realm where human labor causes no added effect upon the Blessed Name, where all proclaim: “Blessed be the Name of the glory of His Kingdom”; and as in the Gemara (Chagigah 13b): “‘Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place’—and His place no one knows.”

column11: Berakhot 58a: ‘Rabbi Sheila said: Since a miracle was performed on my behalf with this verse that I cited, I will interpret it homiletically: Yours, O Lord, is the greatness; that is the act of creation, and so it says: “Who does great things past finding out” (Job 9:10); And the power; that is the exodus from Egypt, as it is stated: “And Israel saw the great work which the Lord did to the Egyptians” (Exodus 14:31);And the glory; that is the sun and the moon that stood still for Joshua, as it is stated: “And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged themselves of their enemies” (Joshua 10:13);And the triumph; that is the downfall of Rome, and so it says describing the…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Berakhot 58a) to illuminate his exposition here (“Wherefore disputes arise in the Oral Torah, each sage discerning from his angle, yet all are the words of the living God, human minds not being identical (Berakhot 58a), Hashem having instituted diversity within the...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: For there is one who perceives lofty ideals yet does not embody what he perceives, and then his perception remains merely in external sight. And this marks the initial entry of a person into words of Torah, as written in the Rokeach: there is no fervor like pious devotion at its outset, yet it exists only in vision; and one requires long exertion until he reaches the state where it becomes an internalized acquisition and all that he perceives is absorbed into his heart, and then he is termed "one who acquires his world."
column15: As it is written: “A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day”; Shabbat indicates that all of creation is still held within His blessed hand and not yet severed in autonomous self-awareness, unable as yet to gaze or exist as an independent entity on its own, and as it is taught in the Gemara (Chagigah 13b): “Chashmal — at times silent (chashot), and at times speaking (memalelot)”; at the moment when the divine speech emanates from the mouth of the Holy One, blessed be He, they are silent and hold no independent power because they are still submerged within His blessed hand, and likewise on every Sabbath creation returns to be re-absorbed into its Source.

column11: Deuteronomy 28:43: ‘The strangers in your midst shall rise above you higher and higher, while you sink lower and lower:’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Deuteronomy 28:43) to illuminate his exposition here (“But being descended from converts, bearing the curse of the convert ascending higher and higher [Deuteronomy 28:43], his body inherited from gentiles had to undergo martyrdom; and so it arose in Divine Thought that...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: As is true for one whose dual exertion causes sin to be forgotten—forgotten meaning lost, not existing in his awareness—unlike the active warrior within whom the foe is present, meaning the outer garment is not inherently clean, the garment being the inclination itself, matter being synonymous with impulse, wherefore angels lack an inclination because they are devoid of physical matter; and likewise one who immerses in Torah and divine service forgets evil and matter, as if his physical body were not a craving vessel.
column15: That is: “Cause of Causes” refers to an overarching root containing future developments, like a grain of wheat encompassing all delicacies made from it later on; whereas “Cause above all Causes” refers to that which is beyond any perceptible relation to cause, far transcending causality altogether; and this is the hidden utterance of “Bereishit,” as taught in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 69, 116b): He has no partner, being One and there is no second, One beyond number (examine there).

column11: Menachot 29b: ‘Moses returned and came before the Holy One, Blessed be He, and said before Him: Master of the Universe, You have a man as great as this and yet You still choose to give the Torah through me. Why? God said to him: Be silent; this intention arose before Me. Moses said before God: Master of the Universe, You have shown me Rabbi Akiva’s Torah, now show me his reward. God said to him: Return to where you were. Moses went back and saw that they were weighing Rabbi Akiva’s flesh in a butcher shop [bemakkulin], as Rabbi Akiva was tortured to death by the Romans. Moses said before Him: Master of the Universe, this is Torah and this is its reward? God said to him: Be silent; this intention arose…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Menachot 29b) to illuminate his exposition here (“all being in justice: for the body of a descendant of converts reaching such height that Moses asked "You have such a man and You give Torah through me?" could only be refined to such supreme holiness through dying...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.

column13: And that is because, although at the start it appears as though a great light opened, within Hashem, blessed be He, there reside vast depths and light far transcending light, so that the initial illumination is darkness by comparison; and Hashem, blessed be He, desires to elevate man at every moment higher and higher; and immediately as he moves forward from the start, this light becomes habitual to him and turns back into darkness and ordinary faith.
column15: Meaning, in these delineated utterances the comprehension of created beings commenced; for in the utterance of “Anochi,” absolute unity was revealed—that there is no existence other than the Blessed Name, all creation being absorbed in Him—leaving as yet no conceptual room to utter “You shall have no other.” And as taught in the Gemara (Shabbat 88b), that the entire world was filled with sweet fragrances—which signifies that the universe was sweetened and refined through the sublime light of His absolute unity.

column13: And in speech it derives from Hashem's speech, which is the Bat Kol as noted above; and in thought it proceeds from Hashem's Thought diffusing through all creatures, its "rear" reflection constituting human cognition according to each vessel. And among the Children of Israel who reckon by the moon—being spiritually humble, possessing nothing of their own like artless babes who know their wisdom is not their own— they serve as a transparent vessel receiving authentic divine Thought, which is born within them exactly as it exists with Hashem, albeit in the mystery of the "rear".
column15: And as in Tikkunei Zohar (Tikkun 69, 116b): at the root of man's form in the lower Shechinah, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness,” so that he be integrated of all sefirot, each of the ten sefirot contributing its share. Meaning that from his goodness he bestows blessing upon all creations, and should any spiritual defect arise in man, all creations unite to aid his redemption through their cry to Hashem: “What will You do for Your great Name!”

column11: Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6: ‘“My mother’s sons were incensed at me.” Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yosei. That is: “I did not guard my own vineyard.”Rabbi Yosei says: “My mother’s sons were incensed at me”—the members of my nation, these are the scouts. “Were incensed at me”—they assailed…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6) to illuminate his exposition here (“just as Israel worshiped the idol only externally [Megillah 12a], all sins of Israel not being true swarthiness, but merely sunburn, and with slight washing the blackness vanishes (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6), and as...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.

column13: And as written in Nedarim (66a): "The daughters of Israel are beautiful, but poverty makes them repulsive," meaning walking in disgraceful attire so that they appear ugly. And as written in Shir HaShirim Rabbah (1:6) on the verse "because the sun has tanned me": that the ugliness comes from an external element surrounding the body, which can be removed.
column15: “And God said, Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree.” Behold, just as a distinction exists between grass and herbs—which endure merely for a single season and not permanently— and trees, which possess lasting permanence from being firmly planted initially, whereupon the sap continually ascends to nourish them, and they reproduce perpetually from their seed sown in the soil without ever ceasing— so is the reality within the human realm: the wicked endure only temporarily like fleeting grass, whereas Israel possesses eternal endurance like deep-rooted trees.

column11: Song of Songs 1:6: ‘Don’t stare at me because I’m so dark,Because the sun has gazed upon me.My mother’s sons quarreled with me,They made me guard the vineyards;My own vineyard I did not guard.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this scriptural verse (Song of Songs 1:6) to illuminate his exposition here (“just as Israel worshiped the idol only externally [Megillah 12a], all sins of Israel not being true swarthiness, but merely sunburn, and with slight washing the blackness vanishes (Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6), and as...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.

column13: And so from the Oral Torah comes the allocation of the Land, expanding without bounds; while in the wilderness the heads gathered in one camp, reflecting their unity in the Written Torah, and from this dimension Moses reigned as king, the Written Torah being titled "his Torah".
column15: And this is what Midrash Rabbah teaches: Had it said “God created heaven and earth,” I would have thought heaven and earth are deities; therefore it states “et.” The explanation of this is: the word “et” denotes a slight interval separating the primordial Will from the manifest revelation of creation; and heaven is merely a garment for His simple, absolute Will; for the word “et” is enfolded within “Zot” (This)—the mystery of midnight, whence all spiritual bounties issue—and “et” cleaves directly to the Emanator.

column11: Berakhot 17a: ‘After his prayer, Rabbi Alexandri said the following: May it be Your will, Lord our God, that You station us in a lighted corner and not in a darkened corner, and do not let our hearts become faint nor our eyes dim. Some say that this was the prayer that Rav Hamnuna would recite, and that after Rabbi Alexandri prayed, he would say the following: Master of the Universe, it is revealed and known before You that our will is to perform Your will, and what prevents us? On the one hand, the yeast in the dough, the evil inclination that is within every person; and the subjugation to the kingdoms on the other. May it be Your will that You will deliver us from their hands, of both the evil…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Berakhot 17a) to illuminate his exposition here (“and as in Berakhot (17a): "It is revealed and known that our will is to do Your will, etc." And Ahasuerus was named because the faces of Israel were blackened in his days (Megillah 11a), meaning merely a temporary,...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And this is the essence of a slave: having no independent head, his master being his head, unlike a freeman who has a head. And his subjugation to Israel is due to their preeminence in Torah and wisdom, hence called "hewer of your wood," Torah being the Tree of Life wherein his service lies. And "drawer of your water"—water denoting desire, indicating that his heart is not cleansed of base desire, bounded in physical deed alone; and his subjugation is relative to "your water," the desires of a Jew being incomparable, for the Holy One is the heart of Israel.
