column13: And this is the light within the Torah that was revealed following the miracle over Haman; and this is the primary distinction between Israel and the nations, for the Oral Torah is that which flows from the hearts of the sages of Israel, and what they innovate constitutes complete Torah. This is not so with what the sages of the gentiles innovate; for though there is wisdom among the nations of the world, there is no Torah among the nations (Midrash Rabbah, Eichah 2:9).
column15: “In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.” This is what Scripture states (Proverbs 3:19–20): “The Lord by wisdom founded the earth; He established the heavens by understanding; by His knowledge the depths were broken open.” “Earth” corresponds to the human heart, as stated in the Holy Zohar (Tzav 28b), and it signifies the diverse feelings of reverent awe that reside in the heart throughout all the specific details of one's actions; and the awe that is present within the heart sprouts from Chochmah (Wisdom) and a transcendent realm.

column11: Megillah 16a: ‘After Haman trimmed his hair, Haman dressed Mordecai in the royal garments. Haman then said to him: Mount the horse and ride. Mordecai said to him: I am unable, as my strength has waned from the days of fasting that I observed. Haman then stooped down before him and Mordecai ascended on him. As he was ascending the horse, Mordecai gave Haman a kick. Haman said to him: Is it not written for you: “Do not rejoice when your enemy falls” (Proverbs 24:17)? Mordecai said to him: This statement applies only to Jews, but with regard to you it is written: “And you shall tread upon their high places” (Deuteronomy 33:29).’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Megillah 16a) to illuminate his exposition here (“regarding which it is said: "shall I not destroy the wise men out of Edom, and understanding out of the mount of Esau?" [Obadiah 1:8], the Sages deriving (Megillah 16a) that one who utters wisdom among the nations is...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And why does the Gemara specify the Flood rather than simply saying that they count years differently? The explanation is that the root of the wisdom of the nations is reflected in the blessing, “Who has given of His wisdom to His creatures”: their wisdom too ultimately derives from His wisdom. Thus the Sages said, “If someone tells you there is wisdom among Edom, believe it,” as Scripture says, “I will destroy the wise men from Edom.”
column15: As we find in the Gemara (Berakhot 56b) regarding one who dreamt his hands were severed, which they interpreted: “You will have no need for the labor of your hands,” and one who dreamt his feet were cut off, which they interpreted: “You will ride on a horse.” And so too regarding the matter of Shabbat, where Tractate Shabbat (73a) enumerates the creative labors of preparing bread and garments wherein man must restrain himself, in truth Shabbat alludes to the ultimate future, as taught in the Gemara (Shabbat 30b): “In the future the Land of Israel will bring forth ready-baked rolls and fine woolen garments,” meaning sustenance and clothing without wearisome toil.

column13: And "Esther is the end of all miracles," as written in Yoma (29a); being like the terminus of every spiritual stature which becomes the head and inception of the subsequent rung; serving as the intermediary between two rungs, the conclusion of the former and the commencement of the latter; and so was this miracle of Purim, although it was likewise cloaked within the natural order; the king having subsequently reversed the decree out of love for his wife; wherefore the Men of the Great Assembly initially refused to consent to commit the miracle to writing.
column15: And in truth, the essence of man’s piercing the concealment is that he implants and establishes sanctity over all the operational limbs of his bodily actions; herein lies the focal point of man’s divine service. And this is the inner intent of the holy Ari, of blessed memory (Likutei Torah, Parashat Bereishit, s.v. Bereishit): “The Torah did not speak in the realm of Atzilut (Emanation), but only in Beriah (Creation).”

Perforce through his accusations he was granted leave to enter and snare them!

column15: And even the fathering of Isaac his son and Jacob our Father stemmed from the power of this divine utterance; for because the holiness within him expanded at times in Isaac's mystery and at times in Jacob's mystery, clarifying the holiness residing in his heart's depth, from this were souls born into the world in this manner.

column11: Berakhot 58a: ‘Rabbi Sheila said: Since a miracle was performed on my behalf with this verse that I cited, I will interpret it homiletically: Yours, O Lord, is the greatness; that is the act of creation, and so it says: “Who does great things past finding out” (Job 9:10); And the power; that is the exodus from Egypt, as it is stated: “And Israel saw the great work which the Lord did to the Egyptians” (Exodus 14:31);And the glory; that is the sun and the moon that stood still for Joshua, as it is stated: “And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the nation had avenged themselves of their enemies” (Joshua 10:13);And the triumph; that is the downfall of Rome, and so it says describing the…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Berakhot 58a) to illuminate his exposition here (“And thence it extends to all nations, over whose sages we bless "Who has given of His wisdom to flesh and blood" (Berakhot 58a), being granted as an external gift detached from God's essential wisdom, for they are...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: Illustrated by listening to music or song: several people may stand together, yet no two experience identical pleasure from that melody; and likewise in consuming a delicacy, the flavor experienced by one is not identical to that tasted by another; which is impossible to explain to another person, since one can never taste another's sensation; but one can understand it by recalling the taste, sound, visual beauty, or worldly experiences felt in childhood versus the perception of that identical item in adulthood and old age.
column15: Yet Hashem in Himself has no need even for this recognition, as demonstrated by the worlds He created and destroyed, leaving no creature to recount His glory. And this is: “Even Noah was not worthy” from Hashem's side to amplify His glory, but that he found grace—this itself being unearned kindness that Hashem desires to make His glory known to flesh and blood.

column11: Malachi 3:19: ‘For lo! That day is at hand, burning like an oven. column13: For they expounded [in Koheles Rabbah 3:20] on the verse "all are of the dust" (Koheles 3:20): even the orb of the sun; which is the highest physical sphere in the world of Asiyah, all formed from the element of earth/dust, even this great luminary; yet it is entirely fire, as they stated [in Nedarim 8b] on the verse "and the day that comes shall burn them up" (Malachi 3:19): that Hashem will draw forth the sun from its sheath; Nedarim 8b (with Avodah Zarah 3b) — on Malachi 3:19, “ki hinneh ha-yom ba bo’er ka-tanur” (“behold, the day comes, burning like an oven”) and “ve-lihat osam ha-yom ha-ba” (“and the coming day shall set them ablaze”): in the Time to…
column15: “I will make you a terror, and you shall be no more”—in this world; “though you be sought for”—in the World of Souls; “yet shall you never be found”—in the World to Come. Israel, however, existed and are destined eternally to exist; and from where is this known? “Remember Your congregation, which You acquired of old (kedem)”—kedem meaning before the world was created; and they exist now, as it is said: “You stand this day all of you”; and they are destined to endure in the World to Come: “And they shall be Mine, says the Lord of hosts, in that day when I make up My jewels.”

column13: And upon attaining this insight Abraham was informed of the priesthood and the Egyptian exile, afflictions being required to clarify why Israel was chosen and the others separated]. And so we find the "House of Joseph," who through awe recognized that all is in Heaven's hands, meriting an enduring house. And conversely we find the "House of Esau," an impure lineage of evildoers even unto a newborn infant; wherefore the House of Joseph shall consume the House of Esau as stubble [Obadiah 1:18], establishing that Jacob was chosen for purity and Esau rejected: "Yet I loved Jacob, and I hated Esau" [Malachi 1:2–3].

column11: Bereshit Rabbah 2:4: ‘Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish interpreted the verses regarding the [four] kingdoms. “The earth was emptiness” – this is the Babylonian kingdom, as it is stated: “I have seen the land, and behold, it was emptiness and disorder” (Jeremiah 4:23). “And disorder [vavohu]” – this is the Median kingdom, [as it is stated:] “They hastened [vayavhilu] to bring Haman” (Esther 6:14). “And darkness”– this is the Greek kingdom, which darkened Israel’s eyes with their edicts, as they used to say to them: ‘Write on the horn of a bull that you have no portion in the God of Israel.’ “Upon the face of the depths” – this is the evil kingdom [Edom], which cannot be calculated, like the depths; just as the depths…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Bereshit Rabbah 2:4) to illuminate his exposition here (“from whom spread Greek philosophy and decrees darkening the eyes of Israel (Bereishit Rabbah 2:4), clouding the "eyes of the congregation"—the Sanhedrin—through their defiled philosophies. column11: Shabbat 21b: ‘The Gemara asks: What is Hanukkah, and why are lights kindled on Hanukkah? When the Greeks entered the Sanctuary they defiled all the oils that were in the Sanctuary by touching them. And when the Hasmonean monarchy overcame them and emerged victorious over them, they searched and found only one cruse of oil that was placed with the seal of the High Priest, undisturbed by the Greeks. And there was sufficient oil there to light the candelabrum for only one day. A miracle occurred and they lit…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Shabbat 21b) to illuminate his exposition here (“And this was the defilement of the oils in the Temple (Shabbat 21b), over whose defeat Chanukah and Purim were established in Hod, fixing Al HaNissim in Thanksgiving. column13: Even to those immersed in the deepest obscurity. column15: Afterward Hashem seals His covenant upon Israel as possessing permanent integration, bestowing the Holy Temple—His seal in this world—manifesting that communion of disparate elements is real even in this corporeal realm. Therefore it was built on high in the Land of Israel (highest of lands), upon the Temple Mount in Jerusalem, because the integration radiating in the Sanctuary is accepted voluntarily by Israel, held not with stubborn coercion; knowing there is no coercion without Hashem's Will, seeking only to recognize that He sanctifies them in every individual action.

column11: Yoma 29a: ‘In tractate Megilla, the Gemara states that Queen Esther prophetically recited this Psalm in reference to her situation as she was about to come before King Ahasuerus without being summoned. Rabbi Zeira said: Why is Esther likened to a hind? It is to tell you: Just as in the case of a hind its womb is narrow and it is desirable to its mate at each and every hour like it is at the first hour, so too, Esther was desirable to Ahasuerus at each and every hour like she was at the first hour. Rabbi Asi said: Why was Esther likened to the dawn? column11: Megillah 14b: ‘Esther was also a prophetess, as it is written: “And it came to pass on the third day that Esther clothed herself in royalty” (Esther 5:1). It is written here: “And she clothed herself,” and it is written elsewhere: “And the spirit clothed Amasai” (I Chronicles 12:19). Just as there the reference is to being enclothed by a spirit, so too Esther was enclothed by a spirit of divine inspiration.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Megillah 14b) to illuminate his exposition here (“Esther derived from "she clothed herself in royalty," salvation occurring through prophecy resting upon her; and Mordecai numbered among the forty-eight prophets via "and the thing was known to Mordecai" [Esther...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.

column11: Megillah 7a: ‘The Sages did not accede to Esther’s request until they found a verse written in the Torah: “Write this for a memorial in the book, and rehearse it in the ears of Joshua: That I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under the heavens” (Exodus 17:14). The Sages interpreted the verse: “Write this,” that which is written in the Torah here in Exodus, and in Deuteronomy; “a memorial,” that which is written in the Prophets, i.e., in I Samuel, on this matter; “in the book,” that which is written in the Megilla. The Megilla is the third mention of Amalek and not the fourth, as both mentions in the Torah pertaining to Amalek are considered one; therefore, Esther would be the third,…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Megillah 7a) to illuminate his exposition here (“and Mordecai numbered among the forty-eight prophets via "and the thing was known to Mordecai" [Esther 2:22] (Megillah 7a), serving as the inception of redemption. column11: Chullin 13b: ‘Rav Yosef bar Minyumi says that Rav Naḥman says: There are no heretics among the nations of the world, i.e., gentile heretics do not have the halakhic status of actual heretics. The Gemara asks: With regard to what matter did Rav Naḥman state the halakha? If we say that it is with regard to slaughter, now that you said the slaughter of a Jewish heretic is forbidden, is it necessary to say the slaughter of a gentile heretic is forbidden? Rather, it is with regard to the halakha that one lowers them into a pit, i.e., one may kill a heretic, and Rav Naḥman holds that one may not kill them. But this too is difficult, as now if one lowers a Jewish heretic into a pit, is it necessary to say…’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Chullin 13b) to illuminate his exposition here (“as the Sages stated in Chullin (13b): idolaters outside the Land of Israel are not authentic idolaters, but merely maintain the custom of their ancestors, and Tosafot there understood that this intended to exclude...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.

column11: Chagigah 5b: ‘The Gemara relates: When Rabbi Yehoshua ben Ḥananya was dying, the Sages said to him: What will become of us, from the threat of the heretics, when there is no scholar like you who can refute them? He said to them that the verse states: “Is wisdom no more in Teiman? Has counsel perished from the prudent? Has their wisdom vanished?” (Jeremiah 49:7). He explained: Since counsel has perished from the prudent, from the Jewish people, the wisdom of the nations of the world has vanished as well, and there will be no superior scholars among them.’ Context and connection to Poked Akarim: In Poked Akarim 6, Rav Tzadok cites this talmudic and halakhic source (Chagigah 5b) to illuminate his exposition here (“and as the Sages expounded on "Is counsel perished from the prudent? And regarding the Persians in...”), showing how the inner meaning of the source clarifies the themes of prayer, barrenness and spiritual fruitfulness, and the Oral Torah developed in Poked Akarim.
column13: And from the geopolitical condition of the world in every era, we can discern the spiritual stature of the souls of Israel in that generation, and likewise the status of the Torah residing in the mouths of authentic scholars in that era and therefore they stated in Chagigah 5b: "If counsel is lost from the children, their wisdom becomes corrupted," see there, and it is understood.
column15: And through forcibly grasping bounty beyond what Hashem intended to bestow—along the lines of “Audacity is effective even toward Heaven” (Sanhedrin 105a) — they corrupted the earthly soil below and blemished the supernal Earth at its root, which serves as the garment for the Land of the Living. As in Zohar (Vayigash 205b) on Isaiah 42:5: “He that gives soul unto the people upon it”—Rabbi Yehudah said: all is rooted Above, and this Earth receives the soul to impart unto all.

column11: Vayikra Rabbah 13:5: ‘Rabbi Shmuel bar Naḥman said: All the prophets saw the kingdoms in their activities.). column13: And from this [heel] is the “grip” of Esav, who “stretches out his hooves” like the swine — that is, his heel; and the Sages said (Vayikra Rabbah 13:5)]’” — making a show of righteousness while [in truth robbing and extorting]. column11: Esther Rabbah 7:5: ‘Rabbi Pinḥas said: Two wealthy men arose in the [history of the] world, one from Israel and one from the idolaters, and their property was only to their harm. When the king saw his wealth, and his ten sons [living] as princes, he arose and promoted and raised him up; that is what is written: “After these matters, King Aḥashverosh promoted Haman son of Hamedata…and he raised him up.” The king commanded that they should bow and prostrate themselves to him. column15: Fulfilling: “I saw all the living... with the second child”—expounded of Noah and his sons who arose after the Flood. For early generations, being close to creation, were governed by rigid laws and vast powers, almost lacking free will; holding immense certainty from their proximity to the Emanator, failing to constrict themselves, knowing their desires were formed by God.

Therefore he perceived the novellae of a seasoned scholar more tangibly than Moses, because within Akiva they were already emerging into actuality, whereas within Moses they existed as pure potential.
column15: And as in Tikkunim (Tikkun 19, 42a): Adam whom the Cause of causes created in His hidden image caused the withdrawal of the Cause of causes; the second Adam sinned in thought, the third Adam sinned in deed; for there are three Adams: Adam of Beriah, Adam of Yetzirah, and Adam of Asiyah. Meaning, to Adam of Asiyah, having become an agent of free choice, the prohibition of the Tree of Knowledge was given, and then Hashem joined the Name Havayah.

column13: All the narratives in the Torah and the Talmud recounting wondrous miracles performed contain within themselves the active power to execute that deed, for all words of Torah are alive and enduring, and within them resides the vital energy for that specific occurrence; as written in Tikkunei Zohar (end of Tikkun 55): from the verse "and the writing was the writing of God" (Exodus 32:16) issues the mystical Name that causes writing to appear; and from the verse "The Lord God has given me the tongue of the learned, etc." (Isaiah 50:4) issues the Name of the preacher.

column13: Therefore, they possess the power to make an impression on the heart of the listener, as is known: “words that issue from the heart enter the heart.” In writing, by contrast, the investiture does not derive from the personal vitality of the sage who innovated that teaching, for that individual vitality cannot clothe itself in written letters, but only from the inclusion of his vitality within the Source of Life, blessed be His Name, of which he is a part, and all human wisdom likewise stems entirely from the blessed Hashem.
column15: When, however, Hashem willed to partner the Name Havayah and form Adam of Yetzirah—as written: “And the Lord God formed,” lower than Beriah—He consulted all creations. And as taught by the Ari: the consultation was directed to the four elements, that they contribute of their vitality to the formation of man. And in the Tikkunim (116b): each sefirah gave its portion — meaning all cosmic forces assisted, contributing to man's formation so that all rungs would integrate and man reign over them.
